title: Post-Course Portfolio: Study Group Web App
descriptionMarkdown:
# Study Group Web App

## Position in the curriculum
Post-course portfolio expansion: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone. This project's focus is many-to-many relationships (a member belongs to many groups; a group has many members) and date/time-driven scheduling logic, which none of the earlier, simpler catalog entries exercise.

## Already-proven foundation
Chapter 12's date/time material already required reasoning about zones, durations, and an injected clock; this project applies that directly to real scheduling conflicts instead of a synthetic exercise, alongside Chapter 24's relationship-mapping material.

## Project scope
Model `Member`, `StudyGroup` (a many-to-many join through a membership entity, so you can record when a member joined), and `Session` (a group, a start time, a duration, a location). Endpoints: create a group, join/leave a group, schedule a session, and list a member's upcoming sessions across every group they belong to, sorted chronologically. Enforce that a member cannot be double-booked: scheduling a session that overlaps another session the same member is already attending (in a different group) must be rejected with a clear conflict response, computed using an injected `Clock`/`ZoneId` so the check is deterministic and testable regardless of when the test runs. Add a simple review/rating on a completed session (one rating per member per session, enforced with a database constraint).

## Required evidence
- A many-to-many relationship test confirming a member's group list and a group's member list both stay correct after several joins and leaves.
- A scheduling-conflict test suite covering back-to-back sessions with no overlap (allowed), a genuine overlap (rejected), and sessions in different time zones normalized to the same instant before comparison.
- A database constraint (and a test) preventing a member from rating the same session twice.
- A `@DataJpaTest` for the "upcoming sessions across all groups" query, confirming correct chronological ordering and exclusion of past sessions relative to the injected clock.
- A migration adding the membership join table with its own timestamp column, applied through a versioned migration tool.

## Review and completion
A reviewer schedules two sessions in different groups that overlap for one shared member, in two different time zones expressed as ISO-8601 offsets, and expects the conflict to be detected correctly regardless of which zone each request was expressed in — then changes the injected clock to a specific instant and confirms the "upcoming sessions" list updates accordingly with no code change beyond the clock.
learningObjectives: Model and query a many-to-many relationship through an explicit join entity carrying its own data
Detect a scheduling conflict correctly across time zones using an injected Clock, not the system clock
Enforce a one-rating-per-member-per-session rule with a database constraint, not application logic alone
Write a correctly-ordered cross-group query and test it against a deterministic, injected notion of "now"
Manage a join-table schema change through a versioned migration
